verdict.rationale: Supabase publishes an official, OAuth-protected Streamable HTTP MCP server at mcp.supabase.com/mcp, with documented tool groups and per-connection scoping (project_ref, read_only, features). The same server runs locally via the CLI, setup is documented for many agents, and a one-command plugin bundles it. Community threads discuss security risks of using it but do not contradict that it works. Missing for 10: fine-grained token scopes for CI connections (docs say all scopes are currently required), independent hands-on corroboration of the connection setup.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server

citations.quote: Supabase MCP server (https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp): Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint, OAuth-protected, for managing projects, database schema, and queries from MCP clients

MCP (Model Context Protocol): a live connection between your agent and your actual Supabase project. Once connected, your agent can call tools to query data, run migrations, deploy Edge Functions, and more.
When using Supabase CLI for local development, the MCP server is available at http://localhost:54321/mcp.
Once connected, your AI assistants can interact with and query your Supabase projects on your behalf.
